determinism.consistency_basis: the basis hash covers schema, context and namespace identity, revision, scope, artifacts, imports, direct-import selection, and declarations while excluding only root annotation extensions and the consistency record itself
determinism.identity: the TheoryContext identity is lowercase SHA-256 of the complete canonical serialized bytes, including its consistency state and non-semantic extensions, and excludes clocks, process IDs, checkout paths, backend versions, and machine identity
determinism.ordering: artifact, import, declaration, and parent-fingerprint registries sort by stable ID; set-valued IDs, references, retirements, and trust hashes sort and deduplicate
determinism.serialization: UTF-8 canonical JSON uses NFC strings, sorted mapping keys, compact separators, ASCII escapes, bounded integers, no floats, and exactly one trailing newline

effects.filesystem: none during construction, validation, serialization, or identity calculation; referenced ProblemIR, evidence, checker-result, and parent-context bytes are not opened implicitly
effects.mutation: constructed context, revision, scope, artifact, import, declaration, epistemic, consistency, and extension values are immutable and caller-owned mutable objects are never retained by alias
effects.solver: none; TheoryContext records explicit authority and evidence boundaries but does not prove a claim or a global consistency theorem

ensures: TheoryContext contains one stable context ID and namespace, one root or derived revision, one theory or local scope, closed artifact and import registries, an explicit direct-import set, closed declarations, one consistency state, and namespaced non-semantic extensions.

Axioms remain explicit assumptions, definitions remain definitional, hypotheses remain private assumptions of one local scope, unchecked lemmas remain unchecked, and checker-attested lemmas retain evidence, result, checker-contract, and trust-dependency identities.

Imported lemmas retain an origin composed of imported context ID, declaration ID, and declaration SHA-256 and repeat that exact origin in their dependency set; no import or declaration dependency cycle is accepted.

Direct imports have unique aliases, every transitive import is reachable from a direct import, imported namespaces and context identities do not collide, and logical or content-addressed self-imports fail closed.

An extension revision preserves every non-retired parent declaration byte-for-byte under its stable ID and cannot retire anything; a general revision may retire named parent declarations explicitly but cannot silently remove or rewrite one.
A local declaration is private, cannot escape through an unscoped dependent declaration, and uses the active local scope; axioms and imported lemmas cannot be relabeled as local authority.

Consistency is only unchecked, unknown, checker-attested for an explicitly covered fragment, or checker-attested inconsistent for explicit conflict references; no whole-context consistent state is representable.

Canonical serialization and SHA-256 identity are reproducible without environmental inputs, while the consistency basis changes whenever any semantic context, revision, scope, artifact, import, or declaration input changes.

Validation checks bounded resources, schema closure, canonicality, identities, namespaces, references, acyclic graphs, scope authority, monotonic revision assertions, and evidence bindings before returning a value.

epistemics.checker_attested: the named checker contract and exact trust dependencies produced the referenced evidence and result for one declaration or one explicitly covered fragment only
epistemics.fragment_consistent: a checker attests only the enumerated declaration references under the exact consistency-basis hash; this is not global consistency
epistemics.inconsistent: the named checker attests a conflict among the enumerated references under the exact consistency-basis hash
epistemics.invalid: one or more representation, identity, reference, authority, revision, canonicalization, or resource invariants fail and no TheoryContext identity is returned
epistemics.mathematical_truth: not inferred from structural validity; axioms and hypotheses are assumptions, imported and local claims retain their declared evidence status
epistemics.unchecked: no bounded consistency checker verdict exists and the human-readable reason remains explicit
epistemics.unknown: a bounded attempt has no consistency verdict for the enumerated coverage and may optionally retain its checker-result artifact
epistemics.valid: all structural and epistemic-accounting invariants pass, without implying theorem truth or global consistency

invariants: The normative schema is docs/contracts/schemas/theory-context-v1.schema.json=6a6e40070ba0a3209f5bfcfa0cc912d1ec08359a178611a40d61ffadda5819ec and unknown fields fail closed at every object boundary.

Artifact, import, and declaration IDs share one collision-free namespace; registry IDs are sorted; declaration qualified names are exact and unique inside the context namespace or one of its child namespaces.

ProblemIR content references name a registered mathhead.problem-ir.v1 artifact by content hash plus entity kind and entity ID; evidence and checker-result references resolve only to artifacts of their declared kinds.

Every direct import has exactly one unique alias, every non-direct import has no alias, imported namespaces are unique and differ from the local namespace, all imports are reachable, and the import dependency graph is acyclic.

Axiom epistemics are assumed, definition epistemics are definitional, local-hypothesis epistemics are assumed_local, and lemma or imported-lemma epistemics are either unchecked or checker_attested; no state silently promotes authority.

Each imported origin and imported dependency includes the exact declaration SHA-256; checker attestations include exact evidence, result, checker-contract ID and SHA-256, plus sorted unique trust-dependency hashes.

Theory scope contains no hypothesis or scoped declaration; local scope names a directly imported parent-theory hash, local declarations are private, and an unscoped declaration cannot depend on a scoped declaration.
Root revision is number zero with no parent or retirements; derived revision advances exactly one step and binds the parent context identity and complete sorted declaration fingerprint registry.

A retained parent declaration has byte-identical canonical SHA-256 under the same ID, a retirement names an existing parent declaration and removes it, extension mode forbids retirements, and every derived revision makes an explicit addition or retirement.

A monotonicity decision consumes the independently hash-verified parent artifact whose complete declaration registry matches the asserted parent fingerprints; the standalone context never treats an unverified parent assertion as authority.

Consistency evidence is bound to the exact semantic basis and sorted declaration coverage; fragment_consistent and inconsistent require evidence and checker results, and a global consistent enum is absent by construction.

Root extension keys use reverse-DNS namespaces, nested payload mapping keys use the closed canonical-value grammar, and extensions cannot override core fields or change representation validity, authority, the consistency basis, or mathematical trust.

JSON integers remain in the portable exact range, strings contain at most 1048576 code points, canonical nesting has at most 64 levels, dependency nesting has at most 512 levels, and artifacts plus imports plus declarations plus parent fingerprints total at most 100000 entities.
raises: TheoryContextValidationError with kind schema for unknown or missing fields, malformed tagged unions, invalid enum values, duplicate JSON keys, invalid scalar types, or noncanonical extension values.
TheoryContextValidationError with kind identity, reference, artifact, import, namespace, epistemic, scope, revision, consistency, cycle, canonical, or budget for the corresponding failed invariant.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit are never converted into an ordinary invalid-TheoryContext result.
requires: Input is a schema-exact mathhead.theory-context.v1 object governed by docs/contracts/schemas/theory-context-v1.schema.json=6a6e40070ba0a3209f5bfcfa0cc912d1ec08359a178611a40d61ffadda5819ec.

Every registry and set-valued reference is canonically ordered, every stable ID and qualified name satisfies its namespace rules, every local reference resolves to a declaration, and every imported reference resolves to a pinned import plus declaration hash.

Every referenced ProblemIR, evidence, checker result, imported context, exported declaration, and parent context is content-addressed; cross-artifact consumers verify those bytes before assigning authority.

For a derived revision, parent declaration fingerprints are the complete registry from the independently SHA-256-verified parent context and retained declarations use their exact prior canonical bytes.

All strings are Unicode NFC without NUL, JSON values contain no floats, integers stay in the portable exact range, extensions use explicit reverse-DNS namespaces, and declared resource limits are satisfied.
